media.caption: A seventh–eighth-century Maya vessel. Its ownership text does not identify the ruler’s polity. Three modern numbered notes point to surviving features on the unchanged photograph; their observations remain separate from interpretation.

items.label: Inscribed forms
items.text: Block-like forms sit beside the figure. The ownership reading comes from the museum’s decipherment; a visible sign is not itself a translated word.

citations.locator: Description ownership/text-image paragraphs; existing main photograph, left side

items.label: Figure and text meet
items.text: The figure’s outlined arm meets the group of signs. The museum interprets an overlap between image and text; the photograph alone does not identify the owner’s polity.

citations.locator: Description text-image discussion and polity paragraph; existing main photograph

items.label: Colour near the rim
items.text: Pale and bluish traces remain near the upper rim. The catalogue proposes a painted-stucco finish; this observation adds no new pigment analysis or restoration.
